title: Nightingale Clinic LLM triage and deployment capture
content:
Context:
- Customer: Nightingale Clinic (regional hospital chain, 6 sites). Exploring Redwood Private to run clinical note summarization + triage assistant behind their VPC.
- Current ask (discovery call 2025-11-17): secure, low-latency inference for short clinical prompts (avg 150 tokens), strict PHI retention rules, KMS integration, audit logs for model input/outputs, and an offline fallback mode during WAN outages.

Attendees (call):
- Nightingale: Dr. Sara Diaz (Clinical Lead), Rajesh Iyer (IT Ops), Mona Alvarez (Security/compliance)
- Redwood: Maya Patel (SE), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Rao (Customer Success)

High-level requirements (customer language -> our mapping):
1) PHI never leaves customer network: must run in their VPC via Redwood Private (private control plane where possible) OR fully on-prem package.
   - Our mapping: Private deployment with control-plane connectivity optional; provide on-prem bundle if they need air-gap.
2) Auditability: immutable audit trail for requests & responses, retention 7 years, tamper-evident logs, exportable to their SIEM.
   - Log retention + signed audit logs + KMS/HSM key wrapping for exports. Confirm retention meets legal.
3) Latency SLO: interactive clinicians need P95 < 250ms for short prompts (150 tokens) and cold-start P95 < 1s.
   - Likely requires dedicated GPU pool (pinned capacity) with warm workers and prefix/KV cache.
4) High availability: multi-site fallback (if one site loses connectivity to central infra, local inference must continue).
   - Edge/offline mode: periodic model and tokenizer sync, local serving runtime with minimal dependencies.
5) Data residency/compliance: EU data sub-accounting for EU clinic; HIPAA BAAs expected.

Important constraints & gotchas raised on call:
- WAN intermittency: some sites have 500ms+ latency to primary region. They insisted on local inference for triage during outages.
- Storage encryption: they use Azure Key Vault and an HSM vendor (Thales). Need integration path or clear migration plan.
- Audit size: retaining full request/response payloads for 7 years is large; they want compressed, non-reversible hashes for PHI after 90 days.
- Model certification: clinical team wants a model that has been evaluated for hallucination rate on discharge summaries (sample set). They will provide 200 redacted examples for regression tests.

Technical risks we flagged:
- Maintaining identical behavior across private/offline and hosted runtime with quantized models. Quantization + compiler kernels can change subtle outputs; regression harness needed.
- Offline sync cadence vs. confidentiality: cadence must be scheduled and signed; key rotation must not break offline deployments.
- Audit export: streaming large logs to SIEM from on-prem worker requires bandwidth planning and backpressure handling.

Quick ideas & config suggestions (SE notes):
- Dedicated model variant: pick an Llama-variant or Med-specific base; use Redwood Optimize recommendations to pick quantization profile that preserves logits for summarization tasks.
- Warm pool: 4 x A10/A100-equivalent per site for predictable latency; autoscale guardrails but with reserved minimum.
- KV prefix cache: persist last-10 prompts per clinician session (helps conversational continuity).
- Fallback policy: prioritized routing to local pool -> regional pool -> fallback compact model (faster, cheaper) with automatic truncation if token budget reached.
- Audit policy: store full payload in encrypted blobstore for 90 days, then replace payloads with salted hashes in long-term index (customer asked for this pattern).

Concrete next steps (owner + ETA):
- Maya: produce a short tech proposal (2-pg) with two deployment options (VPC-private + air-gap on-prem) and cost delta estimate — due 2025-11-24.
- Liam: draft a HA/edge sync plan outlining model sync, key rotation steps, and offline verification checks — due 2025-11-28.
- Priya: initiate legal loop for BAA and confirm incremental log-retention obligations with Nightingale legal — reach out by 2025-11-20.
- Nightingale (Rajesh): provide network topology, NAT/firewall constraints, and Azure Key Vault config example — requested by 2025-11-21.
- Dr. Diaz: provide 200 redacted summaries for model regression tests and a short rubric for acceptable hallucination/error types — requested by 2025-11-26.

Open questions for follow-up (to put in proposal):
- Can Nightingale accept hashed payloads after 90 days or do regulations force full payload retention for some records? (Mona to confirm)
- Which HSM integration is primary (Thales) vs. fallback? Do they want customer-managed keys in HSM or Redwood-managed with key-wrapping?
- Exact throughput target (reqs were P95 < 250ms but how many concurrent clinicians at peak — estimate needed for capacity sizing).
- Do they want model explainability artifacts (attention maps / token-level confidence) included in audit logs? This increases payload sizes.

Notes to self / friction points to watch on implementation:
- Keep early proposal conservative on performance claims; emphasize regression harness & quality gates.
- Emphasize rollback & canary policies in proposal: local canary then fleet rollout.
- Avoid promising exact quantization behavior until we run bench data; include a quantization-readiness checklist.

References & links (internal):
- Internal: playground perf notes for med-llm-7b (link: https://internal.redwood/bench/med-7b)
summary: Call capture + requirements mapping for Nightingale Clinic. Focus areas: private/on-prem deployment, PHI retention, audit logs, low-latency local inference, offline sync, KMS/HSM integration. Next steps assigned to SE/SRE/CS and customer owners with dates.
